subsystems.name: Oscillator (bosonic mode)
subsystems.role: stores the logical qubit as a standing pattern of states in phase space rather than in a two-level system.
parts: high-Q microwave cavity or superconducting resonator

subsystems.name: Ancilla control qubit
subsystems.role: supplies the nonlinearity needed to create, squeeze and read the grid states.
parts: transmon qubit with a Josephson junction

subsystems.name: Squeezing and displacement drives
subsystems.role: shape the lattice of states and control the spacing between its peaks.

subsystems.name: Stabiliser measurement and feedback
subsystems.role: detects small displacements without collapsing the encoded logical information.

subsystems.name: Cryogenics and shielding
subsystems.role: keeps the oscillator cold, quiet and free of stray fields.

subsystems.name: Classical decoder
subsystems.role: decides whether a displacement drifted past the halfway point between lattice peaks.
parts: real-time decoder on FPGA or GPU

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the oscillator
buildSteps.detail: Machine and polish a niobium or aluminium cavity, or pattern a superconducting resonator on a low-loss substrate, until it holds a microwave photon for milliseconds.

buildSteps.title: Build the ancilla qubit
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate a transmon with a Josephson junction, wire up its readout, and measure how long it holds its state.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and cool down
buildSteps.detail: Mount oscillator and qubit in a dilution refrigerator at about 10 millikelvin, shield them from magnetic fields, and install filtered microwave lines.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the coupling
buildSteps.detail: Tune the dispersive interaction between qubit and oscillator and verify the drives that will squeeze the oscillator's quantum noise.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the grid state
buildSteps.detail: Drive the oscillator while repeatedly measuring the qubit so it settles into a superposition of squeezed states arranged on a square lattice, confirmed as a grid of peaks in the Wigner function.

buildSteps.title: Verify with tomography
buildSteps.detail: Displace the state and measure it to map the lattice, and extract how narrow the peaks are relative to their spacing — the squeezing that sets the code's strength.

buildSteps.title: Run correction cycles
buildSteps.detail: Repeatedly measure the displacement stabilisers; a photon-loss event shifts the lattice by less than half a cell and is detected, then cancelled by a conditional displacement or tracked in software as a frame update, without ever reading the logical qubit.

buildSteps.title: Concatenate and scale
buildSteps.detail: Wrap the oscillator code inside an outer qubit code and inject non-Clifford magic states so the encoded qubit can be assembled into a processor.

prerequisites.why: the logical qubit can only be as good as the mode storing it; microwave cavities with quality factors in the millions are routine.
stabiliser measurements must not inject more noise than the code can absorb.
control errors during preparation and readout set a floor on how well errors can be corrected.

prerequisites.tech: Squeezing of the order of ten decibels
prerequisites.why: fault-tolerant operation needs lattice peaks narrow compared with their spacing, and laboratory squeezing still falls short in the systems used.
corrections must land before the state decoheres, so latency in the measurement chain matters.
full computation needs magic states or equivalent operations that bosonic codes do not supply for free.

pathway.milestone: the code, proposed by Gottesman, Kitaev and Preskill in 2001, has been engineered and error-corrected at the single-mode level in superconducting cavities and trapped-ion oscillators
pathway.unlocks: proof that a continuum degree of freedom can hold a protected qubit.

pathway.milestone: higher squeezing and longer-lived logical qubits, alongside companion bosonic encodings such as cat codes
pathway.unlocks: hardware-efficient logical qubits that beat any physical qubit with far fewer components.

pathway.milestone: concatenation with an outer code and magic-state distillation
pathway.unlocks: a genuinely fault-tolerant logical qubit and a route to universal computation.

pathway.milestone: modules of many such qubits, including photonic machines built from squeezed light
pathway.unlocks: scalable quantum processors for simulation, chemistry and cryptography.
